Calculate total fertility and parity-adjusted total fertility rates

Source: R/calculate_tfr.R
calculate_tfr.Rd

Constructs total fertility rates or parity-adjusted total fertility rats from input tables that provide age-specific fertility rates. Input data can come from user-provided input rate schedules, fertility process objects, or estimated rates from a simulation via calculate_fertility_rates, and may be stratified by additional variables.

Usage

calculate_tfr(rates)

calculate_patfr(rates)

Arguments

rates

A table returned by calculate_fertility_rates(), a fertility process object from fertility(), or a data frame with at least age_start, age_end, and rate_fertility or rate columns. Input may be further stratified by other variables.

Value

A tibble with the supplied period and other stratification columns, finite age_start and age_end, and either tfr or patfr.

Details

When the supplied rates table contains columns other than age_start, age_end, and either rate_fertility or rate, the function will treat these additional columns as stratifying dimensions and will stratify the output appropriately. It will also stratify output by time when time_start and time_end are included. The function also ignores additional calculated columns from the output of calculate_fertility_rates, so the results of that function can be directly piped into this function.

When the input rates table is stratified by parity with parity_start and parity_end columns, the function calculate_patfr will be automatically used in place of calculate_tfr to calculate parity-adjusted total fertility rates. See See https://www.humanfertility.org/File/GetDocumentFree/Docs/methods.pdf for details on the estimation of parity-adjusted total fertility rates.

The function will automatically remove any open-ended age bands because TFR cannot be estimated across open-ended age bands. If this band contains a non-zero rate, the function will produce a warning that TFR may be underestimated.

Missing values on rates will result in missing values for the total fertility rate.

See also

calculate_fertility_rates(), fertility()

Examples

# TFR from age-specific rates
calculate_tfr(usa_2000_fertility)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   age_start age_end   tfr
#>       <int>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1        15      45  2.05

# TFR stratified by union type
calculate_tfr(usa_2000_fertility_union)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   union_type  age_start age_end   tfr
#>   <chr>           <int>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1 partnered          15      45  4.20
#> 2 unpartnered        15      45  1.17
